description: A. I. H. Bernal writes to Sabato Morais from Louisville, Kentucky, thanking him for his previous correspondence and addressing a sensitive matter regarding an article in the Asmonean about "the Occident & Revd. Mr. Morais." Bernal expresses concern that the article may have offended Morais and defends his own response by detailing alleged instances of prejudice and dishonesty by an unnamed individual. He concludes with warm wishes for Morais's welfare and requests his address, while also asking about J. L. Hackenburg of Philadelphia and Jacob Mendes De Solla, the newly elected Hazzan of Richmond, Virginia.

title: Letter from S. Morais to S. A. Uhler, 3 July 1874
title2: Letter from S. Morais to S. A. Uhler, 3 July 1874
description: S. Morais responds to Uhler's inquiry about the origins of the Hebrew language and whether the Israelites spoke Hebrew upon entering Egypt. Morais argues that Hebrew and Aramaic were closely related in ancient times but gradually diverged, and provides linguistic and textual evidence—including the homonyms in Jacob's blessing and the distinction between the experiences of Hebrew speakers in Egypt versus Babylon—to support the claim that the seventy persons who emigrated to Egypt spoke Hebrew. He dismisses Philo's testimony as unreliable, asserting that Philo lacked knowledge of Hebrew.
